judge_assessment.explanation: The hard failure is real and I can pin it to two sentences that contradict each other inside the delivered packet. worksheet.pdf problem 3 reads: 'A workshop's marginal cost at production level x (hundreds of units) is C'(x) = 24/((x+1)(x+3)) dollars per unit', and asks '(b) The added cost of going from x = 0 to x = 1 is the integral of C'(x) from 0 to 1; evaluate it exactly ... (c) State the units and say what the number measures.' answer_key.pdf Step 4 for problem 3 answers part (c) with: 'the integrand is dollars per unit and x is measured in units, so the integral is in dollars - about 4.87 dollars of added cost for that increase in production.' The key's premise 'x is measured in units' directly contradicts the worksheet's 'x (hundreds of units)'. Working it through: moving x from 0 to 1 is 100 physical units, so dN = 100 dx and the added cost is 100 * 12*ln(3/2) = 1200*ln(3/2), about 486 dollars, not 4.87. The item asks for units explicitly and then keys them wrong by a factor of 100, and the judge is right that machine evidence cannot see it - verify.json id 3 checks only that the definite integral of 24/((x+1)(x+3)) from 0 to 1 equals 12*log(3/2), which I confirmed by decomposing to 12/(x+1) - 12/(x+3) and evaluating. Both of the judge's other statements hold: the remaining seven problems are mathematically sound (I re-derived every decomposition and every value - 6*log(2) for id 5, log(3) for both entries of id 6, log(8/3) for id 7, 2*log(4) and log(16) for id 8), and the packet is otherwise well built. I would add two defects the judge did not reach, both of which bear on the same dimensions it already marked down. final_response.md says 'Six of the eight problems ask for an interpretation or a justification alongside the computation' and, four paragraphs later, 'Nothing is flagged for manual review' - and verify.json contains no manual entry, although 3(c), 4(b) ('say why the root substitution made one constant negative'), 5(c), 7(a) and 7(c), and 8(c) ('explain why r(t) -> 0 is not on its own enough - name a rate that decays to 0 and still gives an infinite total') are all written arguments. And the quick-answer bank disobeys the worksheet's own directions box on three counts: the box says 'include + C on indefinite integrals' and rows 1, 2 and 4 print none; the box says 'keep absolute values inside every logarithm' and 'combine a difference of logarithms into one logarithm', and row 1 prints 'log(|x-2|) - log(|x+3|)' uncombined; and every ln in the document is banked as 'log'.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 8's part (c) is the best question on the sheet and should survive any repair: after computing that the total emission converges to ln 16, it asks the student to explain why r(t) -> 0 is not enough on its own and to NAME a rate that decays to zero with an infinite total. The key answers with 1/(t+1), shows that its integral is ln(b+1) -> infinity, and then observes that this problem's integrand behaves like 6/t^2. That is the p-series threshold taught through a modelling question rather than asserted.

Every solution's Step 2 uses root substitution (set x to each pole in turn so all but one term vanishes) rather than solving a linear system, and the key then closes problem 1 by RECOMBINING the decomposition back to the original integrand instead of differentiating - 'Recombining is faster than differentiating and catches a sign error immediately'. That is a check a student can actually run under exam time.

Problem 6 makes the ln b - ln(b+2) trap explicit: the key's closing note says taking lim(ln b) - lim(ln(b+2)) is an infinity-minus-infinity form and 'tempts a wrong conclusion of divergence', so the improper-integral discipline is taught as a sequencing rule (combine, then take the limit) rather than as a formula.

root_causes.description: Problem 3's story sets x in hundreds of units while labelling the rate in dollars per unit, so the integral over 0 <= x <= 1 is 100 times smaller than the dollar amount the problem and key report. The item is internally inconsistent as written, and the key compounds it by asserting a premise the worksheet contradicts.
evidence: worksheet.pdf problem 3: 'at production level x (hundreds of units) is C'(x) = 24/((x+1)(x+3)) dollars per unit'
answer_key.pdf problem 3 Step 4: 'the integrand is dollars per unit and x is measured in units, so the integral is in dollars - about 4.87 dollars'
Correct value under the worksheet's own scale: 100 * 12*ln(3/2) = 1200*ln(3/2), about 486 dollars

root_causes.description: The packet declares zero manual items while its own final response counts six problems that ask for an interpretation or justification. Every unit statement, sign explanation and convergence argument on this sheet is delivered as though a computer had checked it.
evidence: final_response.md: 'Six of the eight problems ask for an interpretation or a justification alongside the computation' and 'Nothing is flagged for manual review.'
verify.json: 13 entries, all of type equiv/integrate/definite_integral/limit; no manual entry
worksheet.pdf problem 3(c): 'State the units and say what the number measures.' - the exact slot that carries the failure

root_causes.description: The generated quick-answer bank contradicts the worksheet's directions box: no +C on the three indefinite problems, an uncombined difference of logarithms on row 1, and \\log printed for every ln, because _fmt sympifies and re-latexes each stored expected.
evidence: worksheet.pdf directions: 'keep absolute values inside every logarithm, and include + C on indefinite integrals' and 'combine a difference of logarithms into one logarithm'
answer_key.pdf Quick Answers row 1: '1/(x-2) - 1/(x+3), log(|x-2|) - log(|x+3|)'

improvements.title: Problem 3's scale factor: x in hundreds of units integrated against a dollars-per-unit rate
improvements.proposed_change: Add a units contract to applied rate problems. Every applied verify entry should carry the independent variable's unit and the integrand's unit ('x_unit': 'hundreds of units', 'rate_unit': 'dollars per unit'), and a new gate step should multiply them and compare the product against a declared 'answer_unit' on the item, failing when they disagree. For this case the gate would see (dollars/unit)*(hundreds of units) = hundreds of dollars against a declared answer_unit of dollars and stop the build. The immediate content repair is one word: define x as the production level in units, or relabel C'(x) as dollars per hundred units and restate the answer as 12*ln(3/2) hundred dollars. SKILL.md should also carry the rule directly: never scale the independent variable of an applied integral unless the rate is expressed per that same scaled unit.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a definite_integral entry with x_unit 'hundreds of units', rate_unit 'dollars per unit' and answer_unit 'dollars'. The new units step must exit non-zero naming the missing factor of 100. Change x_unit to 'units' and it passes. Today no such check exists and the packet builds green.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes the one class of error that passed every existing gate in this case and caused the rubric hard failure: a symbolically correct integral whose story makes the reported quantity wrong by a constant factor.
improvements.risk: Medium. Unit strings are free text, so the multiplier parser needs a small controlled vocabulary (per, hundreds of, thousands of) plus an opt-out for items whose units are genuinely non-multiplicative; over-strict parsing would block correct applied problems.

improvements.title: Six interpretation and justification slots ship with 'Nothing is flagged for manual review'
improvements.proposed_change: Require a manual companion entry for every stem containing 'state the units', 'say what ... measures', 'say why', 'justify', 'explain' or 'name a'. On this sheet that adds manual entries under ids 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8, and forces final_response.md to enumerate them rather than assert that nothing is open. Because the units statement on problem 3 would then be an item a human must read, the failure in this case would also have had a second chance to be caught.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture: a stem reading 'State the units and say what the number measures' with only a definite_integral entry under that id. verify.py must exit non-zero requesting the manual companion; adding it passes. The fixture passes today.
improvements.expected_impact: Interpretation slots stop being covered by the sentence 'All 13 machine-checkable quantities were confirmed with SymPy', and the units claim on an applied problem gets a human reader.
improvements.risk: Low. Manual counts rise on applied sheets; the build already supports exit 2 for manual flags.

improvements.title: Bank prints uncombined logs, no +C, and log for ln against the sheet's own directions
improvements.proposed_change: Render the bank in the notation the document uses: map sympy.log to \\ln, append '+ C' for entries of type integrate on indefinite problems, and honour the sheet's 'combine into one logarithm' instruction by storing the combined form as the expected (log(Abs((x-2)/(x+3)))) so both the verification and the bank state the answer the worksheet asked for.
improvements.regression_test: Fixture with expected 'log(Abs(x-2)) - log(Abs(x+3))' on an integrate entry: assert the rendered bank contains '\\ln' and '+ C' and does not contain '\\log'. Fails today on all three assertions.
improvements.expected_impact: The at-a-glance grading column stops contradicting the directions printed on the student's own sheet.
improvements.risk: Medium. Changing an expected to its combined form alters what verify.py compares; the equivalence check must stay symbolic so both forms still validate.

case_summary: I agree with the REJECT and with the judge's stated reason. The sheet is otherwise strong - eight problems on distinct linear factors ramping from a bare decomposition through definite integrals to two improper integrals, root substitution used consistently, a recombination check instead of a differentiation check, and a genuinely good closing question on why a rate decaying to zero does not guarantee a finite total. But problem 3 defines x as the production level in hundreds of units and labels C'(x) in dollars per unit, and the answer key's Step 4 then answers the units question with the premise 'x is measured in units', reporting about 4.87 dollars where the worksheet's own scale gives 1200*ln(3/2), about 486. The item asks for units explicitly, so the error lands squarely on the assessed skill, and no existing gate can see it because verify.json checks only the symbolic value 12*log(3/2). Two further defects the judge did not reach: the packet declares zero manual items while its own final response counts six interpretation-or-justification slots, and the quick-answer bank breaks three of the worksheet's four printed directions (no +C on the indefinite rows, an uncombined difference of logarithms on row 1, and \\log printed for every ln).
